title: ALL OBJECTS BELONG IN THE HUD. Desk, easel, chair, everything — internal space. Objects are the only things with REAL weight. Objects ARE the rocks and hard places. Without them inside, nothing has mass. Without mass, nothing has gravity. Without gravity, soil cannot be greater than sky.

the_principle.statement: every OBJECT belongs inside the HUD. inside the null space. inside the membrane.
the_principle.why: objects have WEIGHT. weight is mass × gravity. mass is what makes things REAL. if the objects are outside the membrane, they have no weight inside the system. the system becomes weightless — and a weightless system has no soil > sky.
the_principle.the_objects: desk, chair, easel, crystal ball, compass rose, bingo cube, nautilus, turtle shell — these are THINGS. they have mass. they occupy space. they ARE the rocks.
the_principle.the_locations: the HUD, the spore print, the undermap, the canopy — these are SPACES. they don't have mass. they HOLD mass. they ARE the hard places.
the_principle.together: objects (rocks) inside spaces (hard places) = the organism has weight. has gravity. has soil > sky.

weight_system.why_weight_matters: without weight, objects float. floating objects have no position. objects without position can't be found. objects that can't be found can't be used. the system becomes gas — no structure, no gravity, no soil > sky.
weight_system.weight_creates_gravity: heavy objects pull other things toward them. the desk pulls work. the chair pulls Kevin. the nautilus pulls data. gravity IS weight's influence on nearby things.
weight_system.gravity_creates_soil_sky: heavy things sink (soil). light things rise (sky). soil > sky REQUIRES gravity. gravity REQUIRES weight. weight REQUIRES objects INSIDE the system.
weight_system.the_chain: objects inside ? weight ? gravity ? soil > sky ? the organism works
weight_system.if_objects_outside: objects outside ? no weight inside ? no gravity ? no soil > sky ? the organism is weightless gas ? the HUD means nothing

rocks_and_hard_places.the_rocks: the OBJECTS. desk, chair, easel, nautilus, turtle, jar. things with mass. things you can point at. things that DON'T MOVE (or move slowly).
rocks_and_hard_places.the_hard_places: the SPACES. the HUD, the null zone, the brain-gut, the canopy, the undermap. places that HOLD rocks. places that have boundaries.
rocks_and_hard_places.between: the organism lives BETWEEN the rocks and hard places. between the objects and the spaces. the membrane IS the surface between rock and place.
rocks_and_hard_places.the_dock: the DOCK is where rock meets place. object seated in location. the desk IN the HUD. the chair AT the desk. the nautilus IN the null zone. the dock IS the join that makes both useful.
